about: The learning page, as one Task Object: what continuous learning means here, the loop, the measured results with their evidence, the safety rules, the limits and how to run it. scripts/build_site.py renders it into site/learning/index.html. Its numbers are measured claims of the learning deck, site/decks/continuous-learning/source/claims.json, and a test keeps the two equal.
title: Learning | ta-amps
description: How ta-amps is designed to keep learning: we re-tune on demand and promote only after evaluation. {{model:muse-glimmer-30b:tuned}}, rose from 93.3% to 99.3% exact-match accuracy on our 150-task tool-call evaluation. Learners turn execution reports into memory, path statistics and routing advice. The loop, measured results, safety rules, limits and how to run it.
heading: Learning
lead: {{model:muse-glimmer-30b:tuned}}: 93 → 99% exact-match on our 150-task tool-call evaluation. Every finished Task leaves a checked result, and every step is recorded. The system is designed to learn from those results: we re-tune on demand and promote only after evaluation. Here is what has been measured, and the rules that keep it honest.
dateline: Results from our evaluation tasks, measured on October 29–31, 2026. Nothing here has been promoted, admitted or deployed.

meaning.heading: What continuous learning means here

items.name: Checked results
items.text: Every finished Task leaves a checked result, and Tessera records every step of how the run went. Workers can add a report of what went right and what went wrong.

items.name: Learners
items.text: Learner runs turn execution reports into memory of similar past work, statistics on which paths succeed, and routing advice. What they write is advice, never a permission.

items.name: Tuning on demand
items.text: {{model:muse-glimmer-30b}} is tuned on checked examples of one job, and a tuned model replaces its base only when a rule fixed in advance says it wins. The examples are made from templates; none come from real work reports.

meaning.note: Learning is Tasks and Task Objects too: an authorized worker claims each learner run and each tuning step, and everything they write is a versioned Task Object. There is no hidden learning service.

loop.heading: The loop
loop.lead: One round of tuning. Each step is a Task that an authorized worker claims, and each leaves a Task Object behind.

steps.text: Templates fill typed slots and compute every label. No model writes a request, an example or a label.
Repeated rows, and rows that match a test row, its request or its template, are rejected with a reason.
Whole tool families are held out of training, and the test is recorded before any model sees it, so it cannot change afterwards.
A small add-on trains on top of the base model. The base itself never changes.
The candidate, the current champion and the unchanged base are scored on the same rows.
The promotion rule, fixed in advance, asks for a real gain and no drop in valid output, refusals or general skills.
The saved adapter, loaded onto a fresh copy of the base, must reproduce its replies exactly.
The pointer moves, or the champion stays. Every version is kept, so rolling back is moving the pointer back.

loop.back: Then the next round starts from the champion, with new examples aimed at its failures.

results.heading: Measured results
results.lead: Exact match is the share of requests a model answered exactly right: the right tool with correctly typed values, or the right refusal. Nothing is repaired before scoring.

items.line: Exact-match accuracy on our 150-task tool-call evaluation, a fresh test fixed before scoring: +6.0 points, with a 95% CI of +2.0 to +10.7. The promotion rule passed 12 of 12 checks.

Answering from memory alone, with no library text added to the prompt: exact match on a 120-task recall and workflow evaluation fixed before scoring. That is 33.3 points above adding 222.3 tokens of retrieved text, 2.28 times faster, and 8 of 8 answers matched after a reload.

A local check with no model calls: across 60 hard search queries over 79 seed packs, the first result was the right pack every time, while the text added to a prompt shrank by 82.8%. Each search took 0.30 ms, and 10 of 10 independent reviews passed.

safety.heading: Safety rules
safety.lead: Every round follows the same rules. A round that fails any check leaves the champion where it was.

items.name: Frozen tests
items.text: Whole tool families are held out of training, and every test set is recorded and fixed, so a score always means the same rows.

items.name: Pre-registration
items.text: The promotion rule was committed before the first training round, and each fresh test is recorded before any model sees it.

items.name: Contamination checks
items.text: Fingerprints reject any training row that matches a test row, its request or its template.

items.name: Reload equivalence
items.text: A saved adapter must reload onto a fresh copy of the base and reproduce its replies exactly before it can be promoted.

items.name: A promotion rule fixed in advance
items.text: A gain whose lower bound is above zero, and no drop in valid output, refusals or general skills. Keeping the base is a valid outcome.

items.name: Rollback
items.text: Adapters are never overwritten, and the champion is one pointer that keeps every version, so rolling back is moving the pointer back.

limits.heading: Honest limits
items: Every result comes from our evaluations, each on one narrow job, such as typed tool calls for Tessera’s own tools.
Rounds start on demand, on recorded runs and our evaluations.
Nothing has been promoted or admitted. A promotion here moves only a private pointer that the next round compares against.
The learners are implemented and pass their tests on our evaluations.

run.heading: Run it yourself
run.text: Tessera’s continuous-tuning guide has the loop, its commands and its tests. Without a GPU, a CPU backend runs every Task and decision and records every step, so you can check the plumbing first.
run.pack: The library’s continuous tuning pack holds the same loop as Tasks and Task Objects, with its own tested code. Like every pack in the library, it is a proposal.
